Primary questions: how quick is it to get started, what's the token cost profile, and what guardrails exist for data retention — we have enterprise customers asking about SOC2.

[00:01:05] Jordan: Totally. For a typical PLG trial, customers sign up, claim free credits, and hit the hosted API within minutes. Priya, want to show the SDK snippet?
[00:01:13] Priya: Sure. I'll read out — apologies it's rough — but cURL to create a client, pass API key, hit /v1/generate, you should see streaming tokens back in under 300-400ms for single-turn short prompts on our hosted tiers — barring regional network variability. Most folks see first-token under a second in us-east.

[00:01:40] Omar: Wait, 300 to 400 ms for first token? For models like the Llama-based ones?
[00:01:44] Priya: Right, depends on model. Our curated light models optimized for latency are sub-1s for first token with small prompt lengths. Heavier models or long-context runs are longer, and if you enable batching you'll see different behavior.

[00:01:58] Sofie: How does the free credits work? Is there an auto-charge after credits expire?
[00:02:03] Jordan: Free credits are given at signup, they don't auto-convert. We send a notice before they expire. The quickstart we send includes sample prompts and a token burn estimate spreadsheet so you can simulate costs.

[00:02:17] Maya: Token burn estimate sounded good. Our budgeting folks want a conservative estimate because some workflows hit high token counts.

[00:02:25] Priya: We typically include a small calc: tokens per prompt x average calls per day x days. We can also instrument a small experiment to profile your actual prompt mix during the free credits window.

[00:02:39] Omar: For data residency, we have customers in EU who require data not leave EU. Does Redwood hosted support region-restricted processing?
[00:02:47] Liam: Yes — hosted supports region selection, and we have EU regions. For strict residency needs we discuss Dedicated or Private where you can pin capacity to a region or run in your VPC. Note that Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and Private is the fully customer-controlled plane.

[00:03:05] Sofie: What's the timeline if we wanted to try Dedicated later? Is it a forklift migration?
[00:03:11] Priya: It can be fairly straightforward. We support model pinning and routing policies to route traffic between hosted and dedicated variants. Migration is about traffic cutover and capacity sizing; we help with a canary and A/B rollout.

[00:03:25] Maya: Security — we need SOC2 plus SSO (SAML). Does Redwood have SOC2 and SAML?
[00:03:31] Jordan: Redwood is SOC2 Type II. We offer SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning on enterprise plans; we'll share the compliance pack.

[00:03:38] Omar: If we use hosted for early experiments, where does customer data go? Is it logged? Are payloads retained?
[00:03:44] Priya: By default, short-term logs for debugging are kept but customers can opt out of retention. For regulated workflows we recommend Dedicated or Private. We'll send the data retention policy PDF as part of the security doc pack.

[00:03:58] Sofie: From a developer point of view, what's the fastest path to get a demo in our app? We want your sample snippet — both SDK and direct REST.
[00:04:06] Priya: We'll include an SDK snippet for Node + Python plus a cURL example. Example flow: sign up, retrieve API key, run a sample chat generate call — that's time-to-first-token. If you embed the SDK in your dev env, you can have a prototype within a few hours.

[00:04:25] Jordan: Many PLG teams create an in-app sandbox. We can also provide a token-limited sandbox key for internal demos.

[00:06:42] Liam: Yes. For Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest and we provide audit logs with event types per request. We'll attach an integration checklist.
